chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and life on the road
title: Joining Jazz at the Philharmonic through Mary McKay
summary: Mary McKay talked Norman Granz into letting Humes sing at an opera house concert in 1945-46, and she became a regular on the JATP tours. She and Granz and Lester Young were also supposed to go into the record business together.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Is that right? That's very interesting, isn't it? Well listen, now after you came out here and getting around to 1950 or something. That's when Jazz at the Philharmonic is getting big, isn't it?
Yeah, let's see, I think I got the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Jazz at the Philharmonic in '45, '46.
Oh, did you? About a year or two after you came out this way. And so what, Norman Granz asked you to join?

No, a friend of mine asked Norman to let me sing with him, Mary McKay. Well, he had a concert, you know, and she went back there and she asked and Norman said, we don't have no lady singer. So she said, 'well let her get up there and sing and see how the people like her'. So the people seemed to like me and so I became a member of jazz at the Philharmonic.
Was that one of those smaller concerts that he started with?
No, it was a big one in the opera house.
Oh, it was. And he let you go out on stage?
Yeah.
Well that must have taken a little bit of talking because he didn't use any singer, did he? And so it went over big?
Yeah.

And then after that, did that mean that you went out on the road with him?
Yes.
And then you made the different records.
Yes. We were supposed to be in the record business together. He and I and Prez. I got the little contract now.
Really? I never heard about that before.
Yeah, we were supposed to be in the record business together. I don't know what happened. (Chuckles) Same thing that's always happened . . . (unintelligible).
Well, it's kind of a surprise to hear that Prez was in on it.
Well, Prez was the biggest thing going.
Yeah. So Norman suggested . . . cause Prez is certainly no business man.
Uh-hmm. And I aint no business woman because I never got a nickel out of it. (laughs)
